courses.title: NEET Crack Down 2026
courses.subtitle: NEET UG — Medical Entrance (MBBS / BDS / AYUSH)
courses.description: Complete NEET UG preparation on the latest NMC syllabus — chapter-wise tests, full-length mocks and PYQs for Physics, Chemistry and Biology. 180 questions, 720 marks, +4/-1.
about: NEET UG is conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) for admission to MBBS, BDS and AYUSH (BAMS, BUMS, BSMS, BHMS) courses across India
Syllabus is based on NCERT Class 11 & 12, as notified by the National Medical Commission (NMC)
All 180 questions are compulsory — no optional questions
Chapter-wise practice tests, full-length mock tests and previous-year question (PYQ) sets
Questions in English and Hindi with detailed solutions and section-wise analysis
courses.syllabusNote: Unit-wise syllabus as per the NMC NEET UG syllabus. Always check the latest NTA information bulletin before the exam.

syllabus.title: Physics
points: Units and Measurements — SI units, dimensions, errors in measurement
Kinematics — motion in a straight line and in a plane, projectile motion, relative velocity
Laws of Motion — Newton's laws, friction, circular motion
Work, Energy and Power — work-energy theorem, conservation of energy, collisions
Rotational Motion — centre of mass, torque, moment of inertia, angular momentum
Gravitation — Kepler's laws, acceleration due to gravity, orbital velocity, escape velocity
Properties of Solids and Liquids — elasticity, fluid pressure, viscosity, surface tension, heat transfer
Thermodynamics — laws of thermodynamics, heat engines, thermodynamic processes
Kinetic Theory of Gases — ideal gas equation, RMS speed, degrees of freedom
Oscillations and Waves — SHM, simple pendulum, wave motion, standing waves, beats
Electrostatics — Coulomb's law, electric field, Gauss's law, potential, capacitors
Current Electricity — Ohm's law, Kirchhoff's laws, Wheatstone bridge, meter bridge, potentiometer
Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism — Biot-Savart law, Ampere's law, moving coil galvanometer, magnetic materials
Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents — Faraday's and Lenz's laws, AC circuits, LCR resonance, transformers
Electromagnetic Waves — displacement current, EM spectrum and its uses
Optics — reflection, refraction, lenses, optical instruments, interference, diffraction, polarisation
Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation — photoelectric effect, de Broglie wavelength
Atoms and Nuclei — Bohr model, hydrogen spectrum, radioactivity, nuclear fission and fusion
Electronic Devices — semiconductors, p-n junction diode, Zener diode, logic gates
Experimental Skills — Vernier callipers, screw gauge, simple pendulum, meter bridge and other practicals

syllabus.title: Chemistry — Physical
points: Some Basic Concepts in Chemistry — mole concept, stoichiometry, empirical and molecular formula
Atomic Structure — Bohr model, quantum numbers, orbitals, electronic configuration
Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure — ionic and covalent bonds, VSEPR, hybridisation, MOT
Chemical Thermodynamics — enthalpy, entropy, Gibbs energy, Hess's law
Solutions — concentration terms, Raoult's law, colligative properties
Equilibrium — chemical and ionic equilibrium, pH, buffers, solubility product
Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry — oxidation number, electrochemical cells, Nernst equation, conductance
Chemical Kinetics — rate of reaction, order and molecularity, Arrhenius equation

syllabus.title: Chemistry — Inorganic
points: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties — periodic trends
p-Block Elements — Groups 13 to 18
d- and f-Block Elements — transition elements, lanthanoids and actinoids
Coordination Compounds — Werner's theory, nomenclature, isomerism, VBT and CFT

syllabus.title: Chemistry — Organic
points: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry — IUPAC nomenclature, isomerism, electronic effects, reaction intermediates
Hydrocarbons — alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, aromatic hydrocarbons
Organic Compounds Containing Halogens — haloalkanes and haloarenes
Organic Compounds Containing Oxygen — alcohols, phenols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids
Organic Compounds Containing Nitrogen — amines, diazonium salts
Biomolecules — carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, nucleic acids, hormones
Principles Related to Practical Chemistry — detection of elements and functional groups, titrations, salt analysis

syllabus.title: Biology (Botany + Zoology)
points: Diversity in Living World — classification, five-kingdom system, plant and animal kingdoms
Structural Organisation in Plants and Animals — morphology and anatomy of flowering plants, animal tissues
Cell Structure and Function — cell organelles, biomolecules, cell cycle and cell division
Plant Physiology — photosynthesis, respiration in plants, plant growth and development
Human Physiology — breathing, body fluids and circulation, excretion, locomotion, neural control, chemical coordination
Reproduction — sexual reproduction in flowering plants, human reproduction, reproductive health
Genetics and Evolution — principles of inheritance, molecular basis of inheritance, evolution
Biology and Human Welfare — human health and disease, microbes in human welfare
Biotechnology and Its Applications — principles, processes and applications of biotechnology
Ecology and Environment — organisms and populations, ecosystem, biodiversity and conservation

testSeries.title: NEET — Most Hard Paper | PYQ Based 2014–2024
testSeries.description: 100 toughest NEET-level PYQ-based questions: Physics, Chemistry, Botany and Zoology (25 each) with step-by-step solutions

courses.title: UPESSC PGT Teacher 2026
courses.subtitle: UP Post Graduate Teacher (Pravakta) — Aided Secondary Schools
courses.description: Subject-wise preparation for UPESSC PGT 2026 (Lecturer, Class 11–12). Post-graduate level subject tests, full-length mocks and previous-year questions in Hindi & English.
about: Conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission (UPESSC) for PGT (Pravakta / Lecturer) posts in government-aided secondary schools of UP
The written exam is subject-specific — you appear in the subject of your post-graduation
Eligibility (generally): Master's degree in the relevant subject + B.Ed — confirm in the official notification
Questions are mostly at graduation and post-graduation level of the subject
Subject-wise topic tests, full-length mocks and PYQ sets with detailed solutions in Hindi & English

points: Physical Chemistry — thermodynamics, kinetics, electrochemistry, quantum chemistry, solutions

Medieval India — Delhi Sultanate, Vijayanagar, Mughal Empire, Bhakti and Sufi movements
Modern India — British rule, 1857, social reform movements, national movement
World History — Renaissance, Reformation, revolutions, World Wars, UNO
Historiography and sources of history

Comparative politics
International relations and India's foreign policy
Public administration and local self-government

syllabus.title: Economics

Macro Economics — national income, employment, inflation, business cycles
Money, Banking and Public Finance
International Trade and Balance of Payments
Indian Economy — planning, agriculture, industry, economic reforms

syllabus.title: Geography

Geography of India — physiography, climate, soils, agriculture, regions
World Geography — continents and major regions
Cartography, maps, remote sensing and GIS basics
